keyframe_review.note: 623,760 km2 for 534-545 (infobox gives no area: page silent). The shape is the post-537 shape: it already gives the Western Wei the western Henan and southwestern Shanxi lands (19 Henan and 111 Shanxi cells), which the Gao Huan page has the Western Wei take only in the counter-attacks of 537 ('In counterattacks, Western Wei took modern western Henan and southwestern Shanxi'). For 534-536 draw the corrected shape; 537 is eastern-wei_537; from 538 the shape stands ('eventually Western Wei troops were forced to abandon Luoyang and withdraw'; by summer 543 'the entire Luoyang region was again under Eastern Wei control').

correction.text: the Eastern Wei realm at its end, the Cliopatria 546 shape

keyframe_review.note: 623,760 km2 for 546-554, identical cell for cell to the 534 shape. Right for 546 and 548; the Eastern Wei ends 7 June 550 ('in 550 Gao Yang deposed Yuan Shanjian and founded his dynasty, the Northern Qi'), so 551-554 belong to the Northern Qi (Cliopatria starts it in 555). Hou Jing holds the Henan provinces in 547 (eastern-wei_547) and the Liang provinces north of the Yangtze come in 549 (eastern-wei_549).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 547: Hou Jing, 'then defending Luoyang and in charge of the provinces south of the Yellow River' (Gao Huan page), 'defected in spring 547' and 'first surrendered the 13 provinces that he commanded to Western Wei, but subsequently also surrendered to Liang'. The rebellion was put down by Murong Shaozong; the page gives no year for the end, the Wu of Liang page has Hou's troops collapse in spring 548.

ledger.note: 534: Gao Huan sets up Yuan Shanjian as emperor of the Eastern Wei. 'In 534, following the disintegration of the Northern Wei dynasty, he installed Yuan Shanjian as ruler of Eastern Wei'; infobox 'Established: 8 November 534'.

region.text: 'modern western Henan and southwestern Shanxi': the Luoyang region and the Henan-Shanxi lands west of it

ledger.note: 537: the Eastern and Western Wei fight over western Henan and southwestern Shanxi. 'Several military campaigns, such as the Battle of Shayuan, were launched against the neighboring Western Wei' (Eastern Wei page); in spring 536 Gao 'made a deep incursion into Western Wei territory, capturing Xia Province' (no outcome on the page).

union.text: the western Henan and southwestern Shanxi lands that Cliopatria already gives the Western Wei in 534: 'Western Wei took modern western Henan and southwestern Shanxi'

region.text: 'modern western Henan and southwestern Shanxi': the Luoyang region and the Henan-Shanxi lands west of it

ledger.note: 537: the Western Wei take western Henan and southwestern Shanxi. 'In counterattacks, Western Wei took modern western Henan and southwestern Shanxi' (placed in the spring 537 account); Gao Huan was beaten at Shayuan in the winter of 537. The page does not say from which side these lands changed hands; the Cliopatria shape already counts them as Western Wei from 534.

538: the Western Wei leave Luoyang. 'In fall 538, Gao Huan, assisted by Hou Jing and Gao Aocao, put Luoyang under siege'; 'eventually Western Wei troops were forced to abandon Luoyang and withdraw.' The year of the withdrawal is the siege's.

union.text: the western Henan and southwestern Shanxi lands that Cliopatria already gives the Western Wei in 534: 'Western Wei took modern western Henan and southwestern Shanxi'

region.text: 'modern western Henan and southwestern Shanxi': the Luoyang region and the Henan-Shanxi lands west of it

ledger.note: 538: the Luoyang siege ends with the Western Wei gone. The battle at Luoyang was 'largely inconclusive with heavy losses on both sides'; the southwestern Shanxi lands stay Western Wei.
543: Gao Zhongmi hands Hulao to the Western Wei. In spring 543 he 'surrendered the important garrison of Hulao', and Western Wei troops came up to Luoyang.

543: the Western Wei are driven off. They were 'repelled in a major battle near Luoyang, during which both Yuwen and Gao Huan were nearly killed'; 'By summer 543, the Western Wei forces had withdrawn, and the entire Luoyang region was again under Eastern Wei control.'

region.text: the provinces south of the Yellow River that Hou Jing commanded

ledger.note: 547: Hou Jing takes the Henan provinces out of the Eastern Wei. 'Hou defected in spring 547'; 'He first surrendered the 13 provinces that he commanded to Western Wei, but subsequently also surrendered to Liang.' Gao Huan had died on 13 February 547 and Gao Cheng ruled.

region.text: the provinces south of the Yellow River that Hou Jing commanded

ledger.note: 548: the Eastern Wei recover Henan. 'In the end Hou did rebel against Gao Huan's son Gao Cheng, and Murong Shaozong put down the rebellion'; the page gives no year. The Wu of Liang page (opened for liang-dynasty) has 'In spring 548, Hou's troops collapsed, and he approached Shouyang', which is the bridge for 548.

region.text: the northeastern provinces north of the Yangtze, approximated as Anhui and Jiangsu within the Liang shape minus the Jiangnan (south-bank) region

ledger.note: 549: the Liang provinces north of the Yangtze submit to the Eastern Wei. After Jiankang fell 'the northeastern provinces, north of the Yangtze River, largely surrendered to Eastern Wei'; 'Xiao Fan gave up Hefei to Eastern Wei'. The pages give no month; the extent is a reading.

wars.name: Eastern Wei-Western Wei wars

union.text: the western Henan and southwestern Shanxi lands that Cliopatria already gives the Western Wei in 534: 'Western Wei took modern western Henan and southwestern Shanxi'

zones.text: 'modern western Henan and southwestern Shanxi': the Luoyang region and the Henan-Shanxi lands west of it

wars.outcome: Gao Huan's incursion of spring 536 (Xia Province), his defeat at Shayuan in winter 537, the siege of Luoyang in fall 538, Hulao in spring 543 and the 50-day siege of Yubi in fall 546 (Wei Xiaokuan held) leave the Luoyang region Eastern Wei and western Henan and southwestern Shanxi Western Wei.
wars.note: The Gao Huan page: 'Eastern Wei's territorial size and military strength was far stronger than Western Wei's.' Heqiao 538 and Mangshan 543 are not named on the pages.

wars.name: Hou Jing's defection and rebellion in Henan

zones.text: the provinces south of the Yellow River that Hou Jing commanded

wars.outcome: Hou Jing offers the 13 provinces he commanded to the Western Wei and Liang in spring 547; the Eastern Wei put the rebellion down and Hou flees to Shouyang.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on the pages. The Luoyang and Shanxi frontier with the Western Wei is approximate; the Yangtze-side gains of 549 are a reading of the pages.

sources.title: Eastern Wei
sources.note: Identity, dates (8 November 534 - 7 June 550), capitals, the 550 fall. Very thin on territory: silent on the capital's move date, Shayuan's year, Rouran, Goguryeo and the Tuyuhun. No area.

sources.note: Gao Huan's wars with the Western Wei 536-546, the Luoyang region 538 and 543, Hou Jing's post, Gao Huan's death in February 547.

sources.title: Hou Jing
sources.note: 547 defection of the 13 provinces, 549 submission of the Liang northeast.

notes: Cliopatria rows: 'Eastern Wei' 534-554 carries two identical 623,760 km2 shapes; the dynasty ended on 7 June 550, so 551-554 belong to the Northern Qi (Cliopatria's Northern Qi starts in 555; the northern-qi dossier should start 550). The shape is the post-537 shape (it gives western Henan and southwestern Shanxi to the Western Wei already in 534) and has no sign of the 547-548 Henan revolt, the 549 gains from Liang or the 537-538 loss of Luoyang. Infobox area: page silent, so the 623,760 km2 could not be compared. NOT SETTLED: (1) the date and extent of Western Wei's 537 gains and whether the southwestern Shanxi lands were ever recovered (the pages are silent: the dossier keeps them lost); (2) the Rouran, Goguryeo and Tuyuhun relations (Eastern Wei page silent; the Gao Huan page has only 'Yujiulü Anagui cut off relations between Rouran and Eastern Wei' in 538), so no vassal events; (3) the extent of the 549 gain (the pages give 'the northeastern provinces, north of the Yangtze River' and Hefei); (4) the 13 provinces of Hou Jing are read as the Henan region; (5) Gao Huan's death is 13 February 547 in the page's lead and 17 February in its infobox; (6) the capital's move to Yecheng is undated on the pages. Page budget: three pages for a state allowed two; the third (Hou Jing) is needed for the Liang counterpart events.
